name: Réunion

findings.local_actor: SRR (Société réunionnaise du radiotéléphone, SFR Réunion)
findings.summary: On 1 July 2021 the Prime Minister authorised SRR (SFR Réunion) under France's network-security law to operate Huawei equipment in its Réunion 5G network; the Conseil d'État upheld the authorisations in June 2022 against Orange's challenge.
findings.analyst_inference: Tier 4 because the instrument is a state authorisation (licence-equivalent), not evidence of operation at scale. Duration of the authorisation is not stated in the opened sources; the national regime limits Huawei authorisations in time, so still_current null. Univers Freebox and AlloForfait both appear to relay the same June 2022 ruling, so independence rests partly on the Conseil d'État text itself.

findings.reversal_of: Orange's request to operate Huawei equipment in its Réunion 5G network
findings.summary: The Prime Minister refused on 13 July 2020 Orange's request under the national-security authorisation regime to use Huawei equipment in its Réunion 5G network, while SRR was later authorised; Orange's competition challenge failed for lack of standing.
findings.analyst_inference: Reason coded geopolitical: the refusal was issued under Article L. 34-11 CPCE, a defence/national-security regime aimed at high-risk vendors. AlloForfait (relaying Capital, not opened) adds that Orange must swap its roughly 430 Huawei 4G antennas in Réunion for Nokia during the 5G rollout at about EUR 43m; single relayed source, so not coded as a separate finding.

findings.controller: Alcatel Submarine Networks (France) and Elettra TLC (Italy), cable suppliers
findings.local_actor: SRR, Zeop, Canal+ Telecom and Telco OI (Réunion consortium members)
findings.financier: European Union; Agence française de développement
findings.summary: METISS, a roughly 3,200 km submarine cable linking Réunion, Mauritius and Madagascar to Durban, entered service in March 2021; a regional operator consortium financed it, with ASN and Elettra TLC as suppliers, at about EUR 75m.

sources.publisher: OSIRIS (Observatoire sur les systèmes d'information, les réseaux et les inforoutes au Sénégal)

findings.analyst_inference: Controller convention (as GLP/GUF): REU is coded as its own territory, so French-state, French-company and EU controllers are 'third'; only actors headquartered in Réunion are 'domestic'. Equipment rule: the supplier is the controller; ASN and Elettra are named as suppliers only in the 2018 OSIRIS article, so the pole rests on one opened source while the cable's operation is corroborated. Consortium membership differs by source (ten members at signing vs six financing members in 2021). Service date given as 5 March (Leader Réunion) or 8 March 2021 (SubTel Forum). EUR value not converted, so USD null.

findings.controller: Groupe Océinde, via Omega Data Centers (THD Group subsidiary)
findings.financier: Agence française de développement (EUR 3.55m non-sovereign loan)
findings.summary: Réunion conglomerate Océinde inaugurated Omega 1 in Le Port in November 2024, described as the island's first Tier III data centre: 1 MW, up to 120 racks, about EUR 10m, part-financed by an AFD loan.
findings.analyst_inference: Controller convention (as GLP/GUF): REU is coded as its own territory, so French-state, French-company and EU controllers are 'third'; only actors headquartered in Réunion are 'domestic'. Océinde is described as a local Réunion conglomerate founded in 1970, so owner-operator is coded domestic; HQ not stated explicitly. AFD (French state) is financier and does not set the pole. USD value is DatacenterDynamics' own conversion of EUR 10m (May 2023). Tier 5 for an operational 1 MW facility; small in absolute terms, but national scale for the territory. Inauguration was Wednesday 13 November 2024 per Outremers360 (published 14 November).
